Skeptic flags:

niche: UHP CW InP lasers + ELS modules for CPO/NPO
scorer_views:
demand 5/4/4/5/3/2/3 pw73: The 2026 demand anchor is real. Nvidia Spectrum-X CPO is in volume production: 10-20k 102.4T-equivalent switches x 16-18 ELS x 8 emitters is about 1.4-3.4M emitters in 2026. Lumentum has a multi-hundred-million PO delivering 1H27, and Nvidia has made a $2B equity plus multi-billion commitment to Coherent; InP is fully allocated with orders booked to 2028. But about half of the 2030 base-case emitters are optical scale-up, which Nvidia still defers to copper (Kyber slip; Morgan Stanley's 6-7M engines in 2027 vs 20-30M expected). I therefore weight the bear 30% (~$0.75B) and trim the base case to ~$2.0B, giving a probability-weighted 2030 of ~$1.7B and a 73% CAGR. That runs off a $0.19B base below the size floor; the niche qualifies on its path to $1B. Most of the headline is base effect: 2027-30 is only ~28%. Tight supply (LTAs, prepayments) meets a 2028 capacity wave, vendor pools widening to 5-7 and LightCounting's double-ordering warning, so cyclicality scores 2. || supply 5/4/4/4/3/2/3 pw76: Probability-weighted 2030 is ~$1.84B (30% bear at ~$0.75B), giving ~76% on the $0.19B base [E]. Almost all of that is base effect: the ramp starts in CQ4-26 and 2027-30 is only ~28% central. Supply is the tightest part of the story today. Lumentum and Coherent hold ~65-80% between them, Lumentum's InP is fully allocated with shipments >30% short of demand and orders booked to 2028 [G], and LTAs, prepayments and Nvidia's $2B equity stake show shortage pricing. I score supply 4, not 5, because the window ends in a 2028 capacity wave (Coherent's 6-inch InP, Furukawa >5x, Yuanjie, freed pluggable CW starts), vendor pools are widening to 5-7, and like-for-like chip prices fall ~15-20%/yr after 2027. Field-replaceable ELS lasers can pile up as inventory, which LightCounting flags as double ordering, so cyclicality is 2. Scale-up optics (2028-29) is the swing factor; integrated and comb lasers are credible but slow. || skeptic 5/4/4/4/3/2/3 pw70: Headline 86% is mostly base effect: 2026 revenue comes from roughly one quarter of ramp (CQ4-26). The 2027-30 rate is ~28% central and ~20% once the 30% bear case ($0.75B in 2030) is included. Probability-weighted 2030 is ~$1.8B.

Visibility is real through 2027: the Lumentum multi-hundred-million PO, orders booked to 2028, Nvidia's $2B equity in Coherent plus a multi-billion commitment, and prepayments.

Skeptic flags:
- Current ASPs are shortage prices. Chip prices fall ~15-20%/yr after 2027.
- A 2028 InP capacity wave is coming (Lumentum +40%, Coherent 2x again, Furukawa 5x, Yuanjie). The vendor pool is widening from 2-3 to 5-7.
- LightCounting has warned on double ordering. Field-replaceable ELS lasers accumulate as inventory rather than being consumed.
- About half of 2030 emitters depend on optical scale-up in 2028-29, which copper, in-module NPO lasers or VLSP could defer.
- Specialist 2030 forecasts disagree by more than 10x (LightCounting implies under $1B; TrendForce-based estimates reach $3-5B).

Growth mix: ~110% volume / ~-10% price.

demand 5/3/4/5/2/2/3 pw63: Design wins are in place for 2026-27: Trainium3's 144-chip switched domain via NeuronSwitch-v1, AMD Helios with 12 TH6 per 72-GPU rack, and an Astera Q3 guide of $540-560M (+40% QoQ). The 2028-30 sockets are contested. AWS has committed Trainium4 to NVLink Fusion, NVIDIA has a $2B stake in Marvell, and Broadcom can bundle switches with its XPUs. Attributing NeuronSwitch to Astera rests on third-party sources only, so 40-55% of the 2026 base is at definitional risk. Content per XPU rises from ~$560 to ~$1,330 on bandwidth while $/Tbps falls. With a 30-35% bear at ~$3B, probability-weighted 2030 is ~$6.5B, giving ~63%; 2027-30 is ~45%. Visibility scores 3 and substitution 2, given NVLink Fusion is actively winning sockets. || supply 5/3/3/5/2/2/3 pw61: E[2030] is ~$6.0-6.4B (30% at ≤$4B including a 10% deep tail), giving ~61% on $0.9B. The exit-rate basis is ~50-58%, and 2027-30 is ~48% central (~43% probability-weighted) [E]. Supply is fabless. Only Astera, Broadcom, Marvell and possibly Upscale combine 200G SerDes, high-radix switch IP and the hyperscaler software stack, and TSMC N3 is tight with XPUs given priority. But $/Tbps falls ~25-35% per generation, sockets are contestable at each XPU generation, and Broadcom can bundle switches with its XPUs, so supply is 3. Substitution is the core risk. AWS has committed Trainium4 to NVLink Fusion, NVIDIA's $2B stake in Marvell adds soft lock-in, in-house or 64-card switchless domains are possible, and photonic fabrics are coming, so 2. Visibility is Astera's guided +40% QoQ and Trainium3/Helios design-ins, but 2028+ sockets are not secured (3). Customer concentration (customers A and B together ~54%) and ODM pipeline fill make cyclicality 2. The NeuronSwitch supplier attribution is unverified and could move ~40-55% of the 2026 base out of the niche. || skeptic 5/3/3/5/2/2/3 pw55: The 73% headline is a ramp-year artifact. On the Q4-26 exit rate it is ~50-58%, and the deep dive itself says to rank on ~50-60%.

The strongest negative is reported, not hypothetical: AWS has committed Trainium4 to NVLink Fusion. Trainium is the anchor socket, and NVIDIA's $2B stake in Marvell creates soft lock-in. GF also expects a 64-card Trainium4.

More skeptic flags:
- Definitional risk: if NeuronSwitch-v1 is in-house, 40-55% of the 2026 base leaves the niche.
- PCIe AI-fabric ends by 2028, and UALink has no confirmed production switch.
- ESUN Ethernet lets Broadcom bundle switches with its XPUs; $/Tbps falls 25-35% per generation.
- Astera's customer concentration (A 29%, B 25%) and a +40% QoQ guide on one program suggest ODM pipeline fill.

Weighting gives ~$5.5-6.5B in 2030 (30% at ≤$4B including a 10% deep tail), or ~55%. Growth mix: ~60% volume / ~40% content per XPU from bandwidth, with like-for-like price negative.

Visibility is good: Lumentum's >$400M backlog, its >$1B CY27 run-rate guide under a signed multi-billion agreement, and multiple hyperscalers shipping.

Skeptic flags:

- Google is 70-90% of demand.
- The shipped-to-backlog jump from $10M to >$400M in ~4 quarters looks like pull-forward.
- There is no price premium. In-niche deflation from Coherent LC, DiCon, Accelink and SiPh entrants takes $/port down 10-12%/yr in the bear case.
- The GPU scale-up leg is contested (copper/CPO), and Kyber has slipped to 2028.

The bear case (25%) is ~22% CAGR. Growth mix: volume plus share shift, with negative price.

About three-quarters of the growth is share shift that cannibalizes PMR at the same vendors. || skeptic 5/4/4/5/3/2/4 pw52: This is the largest and best-evidenced niche: the base rests on Seagate's reported data center EB and $/TB. Probability-weighted 2030 is ~$29B (25% bear at $16B), giving ~52-56%.

The 2027-30 rate stays high (~42%) because WDC's HAMR ramp runs through 2027-29, so the growth is not just base effect.

Skeptic flags:

- The 2026 price includes ~10-17% shortage pricing. Reverting to $10.5/TB cuts 2030 by ~16%.
- WDC is stretching ePMR/UltraSMR (40 TB ePMR shipping), Toshiba is adding MAMR, and a 2028-29 QLC/NAND glut could take HDD share of new hyperscale EB down to 65-70%.

- HDD history is cyclical (FY2023 revenue -37%).

niche: SF6-free HV (>52 kV) switchgear and breakers
scorer_views:
demand 5/4/3/5/4/4/3 pw46: This is regulation-forced substitution. EU 2024/573 bars gear with GWP≥1 at 52-145 kV from 1-Jan-2028, and EirGrid confirms no derogation for 110 kV energised from 2028. The European 52-145 kV SF6-free share goes from ~15% to ~72% of a ~$3B pool, and ~92% of the log growth is share substitution: durable and not shortage-priced. Visibility comes from the law, explicitly SF6-free TSO tenders and Siemens Energy grid orders (+28-41%). Dollars are unverified: no OEM discloses Blue or EconiQ revenue, and the 2026 base is ±40-50%. The revenue step lands on 2027-28 deliveries, so 52-145 kV plateaus in 2029-30; volume above 145 kV stays voluntary until the 2032 ban, and PFAS rules put C4-FN at binary risk. Probability-weighted 2030 is ~$3.2B (30% bear at $2.1B), giving ~46%; 2027-30 is ~35%. Korean entrants compress the premium, so supply scores 3. || supply 5/4/4/5/4/4/3 pw43: E[2030] is ~$3.25B (30% at ~$2.1B, 10% above $5B). Allowing for the bear's higher 2026 base ($0.85-0.95B), my weighted CAGR is ~43% [E]. 2027-30 is ~37%: deliveries step up into the 1-Jan-2028 EU ban, then 52-145 kV plateaus. Supply is a tight oligopoly. Siemens Energy, Hitachi Energy and GE Vernova hold ~85-90%. HV vacuum interrupters at ≥145 kV effectively come from one site (Berlin). IEC type tests take ~12-24 months per rating, TSOs want 2-5 years of pilot service, lead times run 12-36+ months, and grid book-to-bill is ~1.57. Two things hold supply at 4: the SF6-free premium compresses from ~15% to ~7% as Korean OEMs (Hyosung, HD Hyundai) enter, and C4-FN gas supply is unresolved after 3M's exit. Visibility is a legally forced substitution, confirmed by EirGrid's no-derogation stance and explicit SF6-free tenders, plus OEM order counts. The swing is in dollars, not direction. Cyclicality is low: secular grid capex and no China flood in EU HV before 2029-31. The 2026 base is ±40-50% because no OEM discloses Blue or EconiQ revenue, so evidence is 3. || skeptic 5/4/4/5/4/4/3 pw41: This is regulation-forced substitution: the EU 52-145 kV GWP≥1 ban from 1-Jan-2028 is firm, and EirGrid confirms it cannot grant derogations. Growth is ~99% volume (share substitution), with low China-flood risk in EU HV and grid capex as a secular base. These are the most durable drivers in this set.

Skeptic adjustments:
- The 2026 base is ±40-50%. The bear case argues it already holds units for 2028+ energization, which would raise the base and lower the CAGR.
- 52-145 kV plateaus after 2028 (an air pocket after the SF6 rush).
- Above 145 kV, SF6 stays legal until 2032. The UK and Switzerland are not bound, and retrofill gives TSOs an alternative.
- The ECHA PFAS outcome is binary for C4-FN/C5-FK.
- Korean entrants compress the premium.
- The bear case (30%) is ~32% on the $0.70B base.

With base uncertainty included, the probability-weighted figure is ~41%. Evidence quality: the regulation itself is primary, but no OEM discloses SF6-free revenue.

demand 5/4/4/4/4/3/3 pw41: DEMAND-SIDE VIEW. Customer commitments are real and dated. PUCT approved the Oncor Permian CCNs (Aug-28-2026) and probably Howard-Solstice (Sep-2026). PJM 2025 Window 1 and the SPP 2024/2025 ITPs are approved. Korean disclosed 765 kV intake is ~KRW 1,556bn (~$1.1B) over 13 months, delivering 2027-31. AEP says its EHV long-lead items are secured. Unit math: ~35 single-phase units in 2026 rise to ~120-130 in 2030 (~3.5x volume). ASP rises ~7-9%/yr and is locked into backlog. That gives ~4.4x revenue on my $0.27B base. I put the base slightly above the deep dive's $0.25B because the bear's $0.30-0.40B cannot be ruled out, and each +$0.05B costs 5-7 CAGR points. Order-flow back-solve: $1.1B of Korean intake grossed up for a 55-70% share is ~$1.6-2.0B/yr of total intake. That supports $1.1-1.5B/yr of 2030 deliveries only if 2027-28 intake holds, yet 50-70% of the 2030 central is not yet booked. The key demand-side risk is calendar 2030 landing as a trough between the Permian wave (2027-29) and the STEP Eastern/SPP/MISO wave (2030-34). Probability weighting: 30% at $0.8B, 40% at $1.15B, 30% at $1.6B gives ~43% on the $0.27B base; I haircut that for the base skewing toward the bear, which gives 41%. Growth 5 is borderline. 2027-30: ~$0.5B -> $1.2B gives ~32%. VISIBILITY 4: committed capex from regulated utilities plus dated multi-year contracts, but the 2030 back end is largely unbooked. SUPPLY 4: ~5 qualified suppliers worldwide for North American 765 kV, only one US plant capable today, 3-5 year lead times, and test-bay and VPD rationing. It is not 5 because the market is not <=3 suppliers, and Korean/EU capacity displaced by Chinese competition could pressure pricing on 2028+ orders by 10-20%. TIMING 4: material deliveries start in 2027 (HD Hyundai first US 765 kV deliveries, Permian stations), but the 2030 level depends on programs with in-service dates of 2030-32 that can slip 12-24 months. SUBSTITUTION 4: 345 kV double-circuit is credible (~7% cost gap) but mostly threatens the 2031+ pipeline; HVDC is ~0 in the window. CYCLICALITY 3: secular regulated spending with little direct China-flood risk, but concentrated (Texas 35-50% of 2028-30 deliveries) and lumpy. It is also politically exposed (Texas 2027 session, SPP overlay review, FERC EL25-109) and carries slot-reservation and hyperscaler direct-buy pull-forward risk; the stocks are down 61-66% from peak. EVIDENCE 3: primary approvals and DART contract filings are triangulated, but no supplier discloses 765 kV revenue, neither endpoint is observable, and no transcripts were read. || supply 5/4/4/4/4/3/3 pw44: The deep dive's own weights (25% at $0.75B, 35% at $1.05B, 40% at $1.6B) give E[2030] of ~$1.2B, or ~48% on $0.25B. On the supply side I shade E[2030] to ~$1.15B [E]. Three reasons: a 765 kV unit takes ~2-3x the impulse-bay and VPD time of a 345 kV unit; the newly 765 kV-capable plants (HD Hyundai Alabama 2027, Siemens Charlotte 2027, Hitachi South Boston ~2028) carry first-article type-test risk; and calendar 2030 can fall in a trough between the Permian wave (2027-29) and the STEP Eastern/MISO wave (2030-32). I also put the base at ~$0.27B, because the fact-check range ($0.15-0.35B) and the bear's ($0.30-0.40B) disagree and no supplier discloses this revenue. That gives ~44%, comparable to L27 (43) and L03 (41). The 2027-30 CAGR is ~35-41% on a ~$0.45B 2027 [E]. Supply scores 4, not 5. It is tight now: Korean press counts ~5 qualified suppliers for North America; Hyosung, HD Hyundai and Hitachi hold ~75-90%; Memphis is the only US plant that can build 765 kV units today; contracts deliver 3-5 years out (to Jan-2031); transformer prices are +77% since 2019 [3P]; and 800 kV RIP bushings are a bottleneck (Hyosung-Trench long-term agreement [R]). But there are more than 3 suppliers, +50% expansions at Memphis and Alabama plus South Boston and Charlotte cluster in 2027-28, and Chinese oversupply elsewhere could push Korean and EU capacity into the US and cut 2028+ order pricing 10-20%. Visibility scores 4: ~$1.1B of dated DART contracts, approved PUCT CCNs, and approved PJM and SPP plans. Still, ~50-70% of the 2030 central is not yet in disclosed backlog, and the Texas pause calls and SPP overlay review are open. Timing scores 4 rather than 5: the 2027-29 ramp is contracted, but the 2030 endpoint depends on where programs land. Substitution scores 4: 345 kV double-circuit puts only 0-10% of 2030 deliveries at risk, and HVDC is ~0 before 2030. Cyclicality scores 3: regulated transmission is secular, but the end market is a few lumpy programs, pull-forward slot reservations exist, 2027-28 intake could fall 30-50%, and Hyosung and HD Hyundai stocks are down 61-66% from peak. Evidence scores 3: primary DART and regulator documents, but both endpoints are estimated and no transcripts were read. The niche only marginally clears the size floor: the low case reaches just $0.75B in 2030. || skeptic 5/4/4/4/4/3/3 pw41: Growth 5, but only just. I nudged the 2026 base up to ~$0.27B [E] because the bear case puts it at $0.30-0.40B and no supplier discloses 765 kV revenue. I also trimmed the 2030 central to ~$1.2B [E] (the deep dive has $1.25B). Scenarios on that base: bear 30% at $0.75B gives 29%, middle 35% at $1.05B gives 40%, bull 35% at $1.6B gives 56%. Weighted, that is ~41-42%. If the base is $0.35B, the CAGR is ~34%, so the score depends heavily on the unobservable base. Much of the 2026->2030 jump is a small-base effect: 2026 is close to the legacy run-rate of ~15-20 autos/yr. For 2027-30 I use a 2027 base of ~$0.5B [E], which gives ~30%. Visibility 4: there are regulator-approved CCNs (Oncor, Aug-2026), approved PJM/SPP portfolios and ~$1.1B of dated Korean DART contracts [R] delivering 2027-31. Against that, 50-70% of 2030 revenue is not yet in disclosed backlog, and STEP Eastern, SPP and MISO each carry live political or legal risk. Supply 4: about 5 qualified suppliers for North America, 3-5 year lead times, prices +77% since 2019 [3P], and bushing and test-bay bottlenecks. It falls short of 5 because +50% expansions (Memphis, Alabama, South Boston, Charlotte) arrive in 2027-28, and Korean/EU capacity displaced by Chinese oversupply elsewhere could cut prices on 2028+ orders by 10-20%. Timing 4, not 5: new-program deliveries start in 2027, and calendar 2030 could be a trough between the Permian wave (2027-29) and the STEP Eastern/MISO wave (2030-34). Substitution 4: 345 kV double-circuit is the credible alternative and its cost gap is fragile (one SPS estimate doubled). But the approved lines lock in 765 kV for 2030 deliveries, so only ~5-15% of 2030 revenue is at risk; the real exposure is the 2031+ pipeline. Cyclicality 3: rate-based utility capex is secular and direct Chinese entry is negligible (0-3%). However, revenue depends on a few lumpy programs (Texas is 35-50%), slot reservations and framework contracts create double-ordering risk, 2027-28 intake could fall 30-50%, and the Korean suppliers are down 61-66% from peak. Evidence 3: strong primary regulatory and contract data, but both endpoints are own estimates, the full CAGR range is 17-86%, no transcripts were read, and several items are unverified. Profile is close to L27, with slightly weaker cyclicality and timing.
